verdict.summary: You can create an app and get sandbox keys yourself, but those keys only reach Gusto's demo environment. Real Gusto accounts need two approvals from Gusto: Production Pre-Approval and a Security Review. Gusto checks partner eligibility, then asks for security audits or documented controls, and it also decides which scopes your app gets.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours for sandbox setup. Plan on 1-3 days more for the pre-approval form, security documentation and the Partner Checklist/QA build.
verdict.time_to_first_connection: About 30 minutes, but only against a Gusto demo (sandbox) company. Your real Gusto account can't connect until production keys are issued.
verdict.approval_wait: Several weeks to 2 months (reported; Gusto publishes no official timeline)

gates.name: Sandbox / demo environment (Developer Portal keys)
gates.unlocks: OAuth and API calls against demo companies at api.gusto-demo.com using the client_id and secret from the Developer Portal. Real Gusto accounts can't connect at this stage.
limits: Keys work only in the sandbox (api.gusto-demo.com), not in production
Authorization codes expire after 10 minutes; access tokens expire after 2 hours; each refresh token works once
Only primary admins or full-access admins can authorize, and each company has to be authorized separately
Rate limit: 200 requests per minute per access token
gates.time_to_reach: About 30 minutes after the portal account exists

gates.name: No production test-user mode (demo companies only)
gates.unlocks: Gusto has no allowlist or test-user tier in production. Invited testers can use only sandbox demo companies, the same as Gate 1.
limits: Gusto states it cannot support demo or test accounts in production
Any real Gusto account, including a friendly pilot customer, needs production keys (Gate 3)

gates.name: Production (Pre-Approval + QA/Partner Checklist + Security Review)
gates.unlocks: Production client credentials from Gusto Developer Relations, with scopes Gusto assigns. Any Gusto admin can then authorize your app. You promote it yourself; Gusto documents no separate marketplace listing step.
limits: Approval is not guaranteed; Gusto excludes early-stage products without a track record serving small businesses
Gusto assigns scopes during review; calls outside them are rejected
After launch, redirect URI and scope changes go through Gusto developer support
gates.time_to_reach: Several weeks to 2 months (reported: 1-2 weeks per Prismatic, at least 2 weeks per Finch, 1-2 months per a Pipedream issue; Merge says about 1 week for the security review alone)

steps.title: Confirm you qualify for the App Integrations track
steps.detail: The Gusto API is restricted to approved App Integration and Embedded Payroll partners. App Integrations is for apps that push or pull data alongside Gusto's own web app (e.g. accounting, ATS, time tracking). If you only want to connect your own company's Gusto account, Gusto points you to its CLI or MCP server. Decide before investing time: early-stage products without a small-business track record are excluded.
gotchas: Embedded Payroll is a separate track with its own application and review. Don't apply to the wrong one.

steps.title: Create a Gusto Developer Portal account
steps.detail: Sign up at dev.gusto.com, accept the terms of service and set up your account. Merge reports that the sign-up form asks 'Are you building embedded payroll?', which you should answer No for an App Integration.
gotchas: The portal sits behind a Cloudflare bot challenge, so use a normal browser with JavaScript and cookies enabled.

steps.title: Create an organization and an application with the Composio redirect URI
steps.detail: In the portal, set up an organization, then create an application. Give it a name and at least one redirect URI. Saving shows the sandbox client_id and secret. You can register more redirect URIs on the same application later.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The redirect must be an exact URL: no wildcards and no # fragments.
You can edit demo redirects on the Applications tab. Production redirects can only be changed by emailing Gusto developer support, so register the right Composio callback from the start.

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config with your sandbox credentials
steps.detail: In Composio, create a custom auth config for the gusto toolkit and paste the sandbox client_id and client_secret. Composio has no managed Gusto app, so you need your own credentials. These keys only work against api.gusto-demo.com.
gotchas: Composio's toolkit lists production endpoints (api.gusto.com), but sandbox keys only work against api.gusto-demo.com. Check whether your Composio auth config can point at the demo host.

steps.title: Run a test authorization against a demo company
steps.detail: Start a connection and authorize as an admin of a demo company. Composio has to exchange the code within 10 minutes. Then confirm that token refresh works: access tokens last 2 hours, and each refresh token can be used only once.
gotchas: Only primary or full-access admins can authorize, and each company needs its own authorization.

steps.title: Submit the Production Pre-Approval application
steps.detail: From Gusto's App Integrations introduction page, open 'Apply for Production Pre-Approval' (a Qualtrics survey) and describe your use case and the data your app needs. Gusto warns that pre-approval is not a formality. What you submit is governed by Gusto's Developer Terms.
gotchas: Describe your use case precisely. Gusto assigns scopes from it, and Finch reports that vague answers lead to wrong scopes that take a separate form to fix.

steps.title: Prepare the security documentation
steps.detail: Collect your current security audits (SOC 2 Type 2 or ISO 27001), penetration test reports, and security, privacy and data-retention policies. Without a formal audit, document your controls instead: MFA, encryption at rest and in transit, incident response, vulnerability scanning, and a privacy policy. Name a security contact and an incident-response contact, each with name, title and email. An agent can draft the policies; you sign off on them.

steps.title: Wait for the pre-approval decision
steps.detail: Gusto reviews the application. Third-party reports put Gusto's response time at 1-2 weeks to at least 2 weeks, and one report says the full review takes 1-2 months.

steps.title: Complete the Partner Checklist and pass QA in the demo environment
steps.detail: Once pre-approved, you get access to Gusto's Partner Checklist. Copy it, use it to scope your build, build and test against demo companies, then submit the completed checklist. Gusto runs a quality review (QA) and the integration has to work correctly in the demo environment.

steps.title: Go through the Security Review
steps.detail: Gusto runs the Security Review after pre-approval. Finch reports a third-party VISO Trust step that takes about a week, and Merge says the security review usually takes about a week. Answer follow-up questions quickly: the review is on hold until you respond.

steps.title: Swap in production keys and launch
steps.detail: Gusto Developer Relations issues production credentials with your assigned scopes, which you can see in the Developer Portal. Update your Composio auth config with the production client_id and secret, and set its scopes to match what Gusto granted. Then make the integration available on your own site; Gusto describes no separate marketplace listing step.
gotchas: Changing scopes or the production redirect URI later means a request to Gusto developer support.

blockers.symptom: Your real Gusto account can't connect with the Developer Portal keys
blockers.cause: Portal keys only work against the sandbox at api.gusto-demo.com, and Gusto doesn't support demo or test accounts in production.
blockers.fix: Test with demo companies. Production keys come only after pre-approval and the security review.

blockers.cause: The API is limited to approved partners. Early-stage products without a small-business track record are excluded.
blockers.fix: Show an existing small-business customer base and a clear App Integration use case. If you only need your own account, use Gusto's CLI or MCP server.

blockers.cause: Gusto asked for more information and is waiting on your reply.
blockers.fix: Watch for Gusto's emails and answer quickly. The review stays on hold until you respond.

blockers.symptom: Production API calls are rejected for missing scopes
blockers.cause: Gusto assigned scopes from your described use case. Vague answers can lead to the wrong scopes.
blockers.fix: Check your granted scopes in the Developer Portal and ask Gusto developer support for changes.

blockers.symptom: You need to change the production redirect URI
blockers.cause: Production redirects can't be edited in the portal.
blockers.fix: Email Gusto developer support with the change.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Gusto, so you have to register your own Gusto developer application and add Composio's callback as its redirect URI. Composio uses https://api.gusto.com/oauth/authorize and https://api.gusto.com/oauth/token. Your app only reaches demo data until Gusto approves Production Pre-Approval and the Security Review, and Gusto sets the actual scopes, so the Composio defaults may not all be granted.

open_questions: Which Composio callback to register: the toolkit record lists backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add, but backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback was also seen. Use the exact URL shown in your Composio auth config.
Can a Composio custom auth config point at the sandbox host (api.gusto-demo.com) instead of api.gusto.com, so you can test before getting production keys?
Will Gusto grant Composio's default scopes (companies:read, employees:read, payrolls:read) to a new App Integrations app? Gusto sets scopes during review.
Does Gusto rotate refresh tokens? The docs say a refresh token is invalid after one use, but the sample response returns the same value. Check in the sandbox.
Is PKCE supported? The docs only describe the client_secret flow.
